Global Vision Recruitment on behalf of DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd

Date Posted: 10 July 2026

Position: Mechanical Engineer

Salary: $80,000 - $100,000 per annum plus 12% superannuation

Mode: Full-time

Hours: 38 hours per week

Location: 11 Parkside Drive, Condon QLD 4815

Experience required: Minimum 1 year experience as a Mechanical Engineer or in a similar role

DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd is a well-established provider of commercial and residential electrical, air conditioning, HVAC, and sheet metal solutions, proudly servicing Condon and surrounding regions for nearly 40 years. The company specialises in the design, fabrication, installation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical air conditioning and ventilation systems, delivering high-quality solutions tailored to each client's needs. 

Due to continued growth, we are seeking a qualified and motivated Mechanical Engineer to join our team. This role is ideal for an engineer with strong experience in HVAC system design, ductwork engineering, heat load calculations, AutoCAD drafting, and project management.

Key Responsibilities include but not limited to:

•	Design HVAC and ventilation systems for commercial and residential projects, ensuring efficient, practical, and compliant mechanical solutions. 

•	Perform heat load calculations and airflow analysis to determine equipment capacities and optimise system performance. 

•	Prepare detailed 2D AutoCAD drawings and 3D mechanical models for ductwork layouts, plant rooms, and equipment installations. 

•	Design ducting systems, select suitable mechanical equipment, and prepare technical specifications for fabrication and installation. 

•	Manage multiple mechanical projects from design through to installation and commissioning, ensuring completion within agreed budgets and timeframes. 

•	Prepare engineering documentation including mechanical drawings, material schedules, equipment selections, fabrication details, and project reports. 

•	Estimate material quantities, project costs, labour requirements, and procurement schedules to support successful project delivery. 

•	Conduct site inspections, testing, commissioning, and performance assessments to verify system functionality and identify engineering improvements where required. 

•	Analyse technical data, resolve engineering issues, and recommend practical solutions to improve system efficiency, constructability, and operational performance. 

•	Liaise closely with electrical, refrigeration, sheet metal, and construction teams to ensure seamless coordination across multidisciplinary projects. 

•	Ensure all engineering designs, installations, and completed works comply with relevant Australian Standards, the National Construction Code (NCC), workplace health and safety legislation, and contractual requirements. 

Qualifications:

•	Tertiary qualification in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline. 

•	Minimum 1 year experience as a Mechanical Engineer or in a similar role. 

Other Skills and Requirements: 

•	Demonstrated experience in HVAC system design, duct design, and heat load calculations. 

•	Proficiency in AutoCAD 2D and experience developing 3D mechanical drawings/models. 

•	Strong project coordination and project management skills within mechanical services or HVAC projects. 

•	Knowledge of Australian Standards, NCC requirements, and mechanical engineering principles relating to air conditioning and ventilation systems. 

•	Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and organisational skills. 

•	Ability to manage multiple projects while maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and attention to detail. 

If you are an experienced Mechanical Engineer seeking a long-term opportunity with a respected and growing mechanical services company, we encourage you to apply and become part of the team at DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd. 

Email your resume to recruit@gvrc.com.au. Please note that only shortlisted candidate will be contacted.

Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $78,000 - $90,000 p/a plus Super
Employer Name: VD Fire Safety and Electrical Solutions Pty Ltd - T/a VD Safety Systems
A.B.N. 13 662 178 912
Job Location: 18a Durand Terrace, Enfield, SA, 5085,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 13 Jul 2026 > 10 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1696-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client VD Safety Systems, based in Enfield, South Australia, is seeking to add a Fire Protection Equipment Technician to support the installation, testing and maintenance of essential fire protection equipment and safety systems. The role will assist with reliable inspection, servicing and compliance-related work across fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, blankets, exit lighting and associated fire safety equipment.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Install and service portable fire extinguishers across commercial and industrial client sites.
- Inspect and maintain fire hose reels, hydrants and fire blankets.
- Test exit lighting and emergency safety equipment in accordance with requirements.
- Complete routine maintenance checks on fire protection equipment and systems.
- Identify defects, faults or non-compliant equipment during scheduled service visits.
- Prepare accurate service reports, inspection records and maintenance documentation.
- Replace, recharge or repair fire extinguishers and related safety equipment.
- Assist with passive fire and smoke containment system inspection tasks.
- Maintain safe work practices while operating at client premises and worksites.
- Use appropriate tools, testing equipment and safety procedures for each task.
- Communicate clearly with clients regarding service findings and required follow-up work.
- Ensure work is completed in line with relevant fire safety standards.
- Maintain vehicle stock, equipment, labels, tags and service materials.
- Advise building owners about new fire protection equipment and systems as per industry standard.
- Support scheduled servicing programmes and urgent repair or maintenance requests .
- Capacity to work independently across client locations while maintaining safe, industry standard and professional work practices.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- AQF Certificate III including at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV or at least three years of relevant experience.
- Ability to inspect, service and maintain extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants and related equipment.
- Sound understanding of fire safety procedures, compliance requirements and accurate service documentation practices.
- Practical ability to identify equipment faults, defects and maintenance requirements during site inspections.
- Capacity to work independently to industry standards across client locations while maintaining safe and professional work practices.
- Good communication skills to explain service findings, required repairs and maintenance outcomes to clients.
- Current driver licence and willingness to travel to different commercial and industrial worksites as required.
- Ability to use relevant tools, testing equipment, labels and service materials accurately and safely.

Please include Reference: J1696-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

The Diesel Motor Mechanics are responsible for the inspection, diagnosis, repair, and maintenance of heavy diesel-powered vehicles and equipment.  Play a key role in supporting the successful delivery of community infrastructure and operational projects by providing contract administration, contractor payment and procurement support within a structured local government environment. 
  Your new opportunity  
 This Mackay-based opportunity sits within a collaborative Procurement team responsible for supporting contract management activities across a diverse portfolio of capital works and operational projects. Working closely with Project Managers, Finance and contractors, you will help ensure contracts are administered effectively, risks are managed appropriately, and contractor payments are processed accurately and in accordance with legislative and contractual requirements. 
 This role is well suited to a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working across multiple stakeholders, maintaining accurate records and contributing to the successful delivery of projects and procurement outcomes. 
  Your new role  
 As the Contracts Administration Officer, you will provide essential administrative and commercial support across Council's contractor management and procurement functions. 
 In this role you will: 
 
 Support the implementation and administration of contractor management processes in accordance with Council policies, procedures and standards 
 Assist Project Managers with maintaining accurate project costing records, forecasting and job costing information 
 Coordinate and assist with the assessment and preparation of contractor payment claims 
 Process contractor payments in accordance with contractual obligations and legislative timeframes 
 Assist with the assessment of variation claims, including documentation, negotiations and notifications 
 Prepare and maintain contract variations and associated contract documentation 
 Ensure all contract-related records are accurate, current and managed in accordance with record-keeping and retention requirements 
 Maintain accurate information within contracts management and financial systems 
 Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across procurement and contractor management processes 
 Liaise effectively with Project Managers, Finance teams and contractors to support successful project delivery 
 
 This is a hands-on role where attention to detail, organisation and strong stakeholder engagement skills are critical to success. 
  What you'll need to succeed  
 You will bring strong administrative and contract management experience, along with the ability to manage competing priorities within a fast-paced project environment. 
 Key requirements include: 
 
 Experience processing invoices and contractor payment claims within required timeframes 
 Demonstrated experience in a contract administration or similar role 
 Experience using contract management and financial systems such as SAP, TechnologyOne, CiAnywhere or similar platforms 
 Strong Microsoft Office skills 
 Understanding of contract management processes, contract law and relevant legislation 
 Knowledge of the Building Industry Fairness (Security of Payment) Act 2017 
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate documentation and records 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships 
 Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload 
 
 Desirable: 
 
 Certificate III in Business Administration or a related qualification 
 Experience within Local Government or capital works environments 
 Experience supporting procurement and contractor management activities 
 Experience maintaining and reporting within corporate financial management systems 
 Knowledge of Local Government procurement legislation, policies and procedures 
 Commercial acumen and an understanding of the financial aspects of contracts 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 You'll be joining a supportive local government environment where your work directly contributes to the delivery of important projects and services for the community. 
 In return, you will enjoy: 
 
 A stable and rewarding opportunity within Local Government 
 Exposure to a broad range of infrastructure and operational projects 
 A collaborative and professional team environment 
 Opportunities to further develop procurement, contract administration and project support capabilities 
 The chance to work closely with a variety of stakeholders across Council and contractor networks 
 A role where accuracy, organisation and attention to detail are highly valued 
 
  What you need to do now
